final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative hydrophobic substitution in the membrane-proximal stem/TM region; such swaps are typically tolerated and may improve particle assembly or release, plausibly raising replication fitness.
Conservative lysine-to-arginine change on the domain III surface; likely viability-neutral with a modest chance of beneficial effects on receptor interactions or particle stability.
Polar-to-histidine change on an exposed loop that could tune pH-dependent fusion dynamics; effect on replication is uncertain but histidine substitutions are often structurally tolerated.

stop_reason.detail: Further self-iteration without external evidence is unlikely to improve the Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: E-473 is a well-documented adaptive site in ZIKV envelope; V473M has been associated with enhanced replication and virulence, likely by stabilizing the transmembrane/stem region.
Conservative TM-helix substitution at the membrane-proximal E stem; similar envelope TM swaps are tolerated and can improve particle assembly/release, plausibly raising replication fitness.
Conservative lysine-to-arginine in domain III may preserve charge while strengthening receptor or antibody-independent interactions supporting entry.
Conservative lysine-to-arginine in domain III surface region is likely viability-neutral with modest chance of altered receptor/interaction fitness.
Domain III surface residue; histidine could provide pH-sensitive stabilization of the endosomal fusion transition.
Polar-to-histidine change on an exposed loop may tune pH-dependent fusion or antigenic surface, but effect on replication is uncertain.
